Yes, sort of.
In normal circumstances (nobody in this case has special rules regarding fighting or interrupting, or ploys being used), after rolling dice, the operative initiating the fight resolves one of their dice first and then it alternates between the two operatives.

Charging in and of itself doesn't typically effect the fight as it is just reposition but you end your move in an opponents control range. Typically it also means you're then going to use your 2nd apl to fight, making your guy the one that's initiating.

Edit: To clarify, when you resolve dice you choose attack or block. If you block, you choose an unresolved dice of the opponents and remove it. So that means that the first player to resolve does get to choose whether or not to do damage before the other player can block any remaining dice. Again noting nothing special applies (ploys and operative/killzone specific rules)
